annotations.text:
Same theme, new structure.

The old dashboard put five horizontally-scrolling tabs under four KPI cards, and every card had its own coloured icon chip. That is where the mess came from — four accent colours competing before you had read a single number.

What changed:
• A left sidebar, grouped Run the shop / Grow / Money. Room for nine sections instead of five, no horizontal scroll.
• Colour is now reserved. Orange means "a thing to act on". Status colours are the existing StatusPill palette and nothing else borrows them.
• The KPI row is one flat strip, not four floating cards.

Needs you today — the biggest change.

The old Overview opened with vanity totals. A seller's actual first question is "what do I have to do?", so the top of Home is now a queue: orders to ship, deliveries waiting on an OTP, stock about to run out, and whether the bank account is verified.

Empty queue = nothing to do today. That is the goal state.

Added, not in the app yet:

Customers · Insights · Discounts · Storefront appearance · bulk order actions and CSV export · packing slips · low-stock forecasting ("runs out Thursday") · payout history with commission per settlement · delivery charges and free-delivery threshold · GSTIN and HSN fields · notification preferences.

All the numbers on these boards are sample data.

Most of these sellers run the shop from a phone.

Home is the same action queue, thumb-reachable. The second board is the doorstep moment: the seller has the parcel in one hand and needs to type the buyer's 6-digit code — so that is the whole screen, with 56px inputs and a 52px button.

No fake status bar or keyboard: the real ones render on top.
